stem: Which principle should guide routine preoperative testing for an adult having elective surgery?

options.A: Use the same laboratory and diagnostic panel for every client so preoperative testing is standardized regardless of health or surgery type.
options.B: Order tests even when the result is unlikely to affect perioperative planning because routine testing should be independent of clinical indication.
options.C: Use test results in place of a preoperative history, medication review, physical assessment, and evaluation of procedure-related risk.
options.D: Select tests according to the client's health, comorbidities, medicines, ASA grade, and surgery type when the information can influence perioperative care.

rationale: Current NICE NG45 guidance aims to reduce unnecessary preoperative testing and varies recommendations according to surgery grade, ASA grade, comorbidities, medicines, and specific clinical indications. It explicitly advises against routine chest X-ray, resting echocardiography, urine dipstick, and many laboratory tests in low-risk situations, while recommending or considering selected tests for higher-risk patients or procedures. Therefore D is correct. A imposes a blanket panel, B ignores whether testing is clinically useful, and C incorrectly substitutes testing for the preoperative clinical assessment.
educational_objective: Use individualized clinical indications rather than blanket test panels when considering routine preoperative testing.
source_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
source_document_title: NG45 — Routine preoperative tests for elective surgery
source_version_date: Published April 5, 2016; current NICE guidance and resources live-rechecked 2026-08-26
source_locator: Overview: reduce unnecessary testing; choice depends on comorbidities and surgery. Recommendations 1.2.1: consider medicines; 1.5-1.9: several tests not routinely offered without indication; tables for minor/intermediate/major-complex surgery vary tests by ASA grade and comorbidity. Public information: needed tests depend mainly on health and type of anesthesia/surgery.
source_claim_supported: Preoperative testing should be individualized according to health/comorbidities, medicines, ASA/surgery grade, and whether results can affect management rather than using one universal panel.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — preoperative assessment and interpretation of diagnostic testing.
correction_summary: Balanced option lengths and retained individualized preoperative testing as the uniquely correct principle.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — current NICE recommendations repeatedly vary testing by surgery/ASA/comorbidity and explicitly avoid many routine tests; D uniquely matches the guideline framework.
